title: Katsura: Ancient Katsura Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: A Japanese forest tree whose falling leaves smell of burnt sugar. The Great Katsura of Itoi is a ring of about eighty stems over 18 metres round.
intro: Katsura grows wild in the old forests of Japan, and its oldest trees rarely keep their first trunk. The Great Katsura of Itoi, in a gorge near Asago, is a hollow stump ringed by roughly eighty root suckers, over 18 metres round together and put at more than a thousand years; a travelling priest is said to have draped his robe over it and prayed for rain. At the Koganeyu hot spring in Sapporo, a katsura became a god, worshipped as Fudo Myoo standing in tree form. The species travels well. The Sapporo Katsuras in Boston grew from seed William S. Clark sent from Japan to the Arnold Arboretum in 1878. Every October the yellowing leaves give off maltol, and the ground under a katsura from Gdansk to Pittsburgh smells of burnt sugar.
